en: When Mayon Volcano shows unrest, residents within its six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone must evacuate to avoid lethal pyroclastic flows.
After typhoon floods, avoid wading in contaminated water to prevent leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection spread by rat urine.
If you feel a strong earthquake near the coast, immediately walk to higher ground because a tsunami might follow.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must wear thick jackets because temperatures at its summit can drop to near freezing.
When swimming at Philippine beaches, always swim parallel to the shore if caught in a strong, narrow rip current.
While trekking in the Sierra Madre mountains, wear long pants and tucked socks to prevent painful leech bites.
Apply sunscreen when visiting Boracay because the white sand reflects ultraviolet rays, increasing your risk of severe sunburns.
During heavy monsoon rains in the Cordillera mountains, stay away from steep slopes to avoid deadly landslides.
Wear an N95 mask when Taal Volcano emits ashfall to prevent fine volcanic particles from damaging your lungs.
Never swim in the Cagayan River during the rainy season because sudden upstream rains can cause flash floods.
Always boil water from natural mountain springs before drinking to kill harmful bacteria and prevent stomach illnesses.
If you encounter a Philippine cobra in rural fields, freeze and back away slowly to avoid its highly venomous bite.
